transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-30 16:00 PT | Duration: ~44 mins | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Maya (CascadeHealth Procurement), Priya (Cascade Legal), Alan (CTO), Jon (Platform)

Summary: Procurement and legal walk-through of MSA and DPA items, SLA specifics for latency and uptime, pricing approvals needed for pilot, and next steps for onboarding.

00:00 Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll run through the MSA and DPA items you sent and then talk SLAs and pilot onboarding, sound good?
00:05 Maya: yes thanks Samira, we only have about 45 minutes so appreciate the tight agenda.
00:12 Ethan: quick intro from me, I'm Ethan on the SE side; I'll cover the SLA and infra notes and then Lina will cover onboarding flow.
00:20 Priya: great, just to flag our legal team already redlined section 7 on liability and 9 on data processing, and we have concerns about retention and audit logs in the DPA.
00:32 Samira: okay helpful — can you share the redline directly in the thread after this, that helps us prepare. for SLA, we've proposed 99.99 uptime on Redwood Dedicated and 99.9 on hosted with latency SLOs per model, let me walk through specifics.
00:48 Jon: quick Q — CascadeHealth requires data residency in us-east-1 and logs retained for 7 years for audits; is that supported in hosted or do we need a private deployment?
00:58 Ethan: short answer: we support region pinning on hosted for data residency, and we have Private (VPC) deployments for strict residency/air-gapped needs; audit log retention can be configured with our log export into their storage, we'll include KMS integration notes in the pack.
01:12 Maya: procurement will want the DPA to explicitly state log retention and access policies, and KMS control for customer-managed keys.
01:20 Samira: yes we'll add explicit language around KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys in the DPA redline.
01:30 Priya: liability caps — our legal wants to see a cap tied to fees paid in 12 months; your MSA currently has a higher cap. also indemnity for PHI exposures is sensitive.
01:45 Samira: understoood — we can propose a compromise, i'll review our standard cap and propose options; on PHI we have BAAs available though they are a separate addendum, i can loop in the compliance team.
01:58 Ethan: from a technical SLA perspective, we recommend Dedicated for production workflows that require consistent p99 latency under 500ms and throughput guarantees; hosted is fine for lower-criticality features and has a lower price point.
02:14 Alan: our primary metric is p95 latency under 250ms for the interactive clinical UI, p99 less critical but we'd like it under 700ms. can Dedicated meet 250 p95?
02:28 Ethan: yes on modern A100/H100 profiles with optimized batching and KV cache we can meet 250ms p95 for short prompts; we will need to align on prompt length and token volumes in the pilot.
02:40 Jon: what's the fallback if Dedicated capacity is constrained — do you have automatic fallback to a hosted variant?
02:48 Ethan: yes we support routing policies that will fallback to a compatible hosted model variant; we can configure strict failover rules and can also do a canary split.
02:58 Maya: pricing — procurement needs clear tiers; we need to know the per-token or per-call pricing for hosted vs Dedicated reserved, and the breakpoints for discounts.
03:12 Samira: we have three tiers: hosted (pay-as-you-go), dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit), and private (enterprise license). i'll send the pricing sheet showing per-token/embedding rates and discount thresholds for commits — typical discounts start at $X/month commit, i'll include examples.
03:30 Priya: procurement will also need a pricing validity window and an approval stamp from sales manager for anything over $100k annual spend.
03:38 Samira: understood, i'll include approval sign-off and a proposed timeline for pricing lock.
03:44 Maya: timeline wise, we need procurement approval by mid-May to start a pilot in late May, legal signoff ideally the week after. is that achievable?
03:58 Samira: that's tight but possible; we should get the MSA redline back within a week and security docs within 4 business days, then schedule the pilot onboarding call targeting week of May 11th.
04:10 Ethan: for pilot success criteria — recommend we define throughput targets, latency SLOs, dataset boundaries, and a small eval prompt set; Lina will prepare a checklist.
04:22 Lina: i'll put together a pilot checklist and an eval template (example prompts, baseline metrics) and share with Jon and Alan.
04:30 Priya: regarding DPA, please clarify subprocessors and any third-party logging providers. we need vendor lists.
04:38 Ethan: we'll include subprocessors list and notes on where logs are stored, and you can push for SOC2 evidence which we will provide.
04:46 Maya: can we get a copy of your SOC2 report and the last penetration test summary?
04:52 Samira: yes we'll include SOC2 Type II report and a high level pen test summary in the security pack; for full reports we'll do an NDA gated share if needed.
05:05 Jon: small technical note — we plan to use your API for embeddings and chat generation; what about throughput caps and burst?
05:14 Ethan: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity options; we'll propose a recommended VM/GPU profile for your expected RPS in the pricing worksheet.
05:26 Priya: legal also wants SLAs tied to credits for downtime, not just vague statements. can you add explicit SLA credit terms?
05:34 Samira: yes we'll propose specific credit tables for different uptime tiers and include remedy language; we can map to your suggested cap.
05:44 Maya: any integration work required from our infra team for pilot?
05:50 Ethan: for hosted pilot minimal; for Private/VPC you'll need network peering and configuration; for hosted we ask for API keys, sample dataset, and some test endpoints for load testing.
06:03 Jon: who manages encryption keys if we choose hosted? we prefer customer-managed keys.
06:10 Ethan: supported — we integrate with customer KMS for key management, outline in the DPA and deployment guide.
06:20 Priya: can you call out data deletion timelines and proof of deletion in the DPA?
06:26 Samira: yes we'll add data deletion clauses and procedures for proof of deletion.
06:33 Maya: procurement will need a single point of contact on Redwood's side for procurement/legal follow-up.
06:40 Samira: that'll be me, i'll be the procurement owner and lina will handle onboarding logistics.
06:46 Lina: noted — i'll coordinate the pilot checklist and schedule.
06:52 Priya: one more from legal — please include audit log schema examples and access controls (RBAC) in the security pack.
07:00 Ethan: will include log schema, retention controls, and RBAC notes with examples of roles and permissions.
07:10 Maya: ok good — if we get the MSA redline and security pack by next week procurement can review and hopefully approve by 5/15.
07:20 Samira: we'll aim for that.
07:25 Alan: for the pilot can we lock a model version so we don't get noisy regression changes?
07:30 Ethan: absolutely — we support pinning model versions and rollout policies; we'll show how to pin a version in the onboarding doc.
07:38 Jon: any PCI/PHI specific compliance we should be aware of? we handle PHI in parts of the product so BAAs are required.
07:45 Samira: BAAs are handled as an addendum — we'll surface the BAA workflow and sample language; compliance team will follow up.
07:53 Maya: last question — do you support audit logging to our S3 for long term retention?
08:00 Ethan: yes we support log export to customer S3 buckets with lifecycle policies, we'll document steps.
08:08 Samira: ok i'm going to recap next steps: i'll send updated MSA redline with SLA table and credit language, ethan will send security pack (SOC2, pen test summary, KMS notes), lina will draft pilot checklist and success criteria, priya will send legal redlines. we'll aim to reconvene after docs are in place, target pilot kickoff week of May 11.
08:28 Maya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
08:33 Samira: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments and a calendar invite for the onboarding call. bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard words and name variants (e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as K-V cash), some filler words and overlaps.
